name: Stipendium Hungaricum
tagline: Hungary's flagship government scholarship — tuition-free study for students from partner countries.
fields: Around 900 programmes across most fields, taught mainly in English (some in Hungarian, a few in German or French). Which programmes you can choose depends on your sending country — check the official Study Finder.

stipend.text: Monthly stipend — Bachelor's / Master's / one-tier / non-degree: HUF 43,700 (~€110). PhD Phase 1: HUF 140,000 (~€355). PhD Phase 2: HUF 180,000 (~€460).

accommodation.text: Free dormitory place, OR a HUF 40,000/month (~€100) housing contribution. Officially noted this often does not cover full rent in larger cities like Budapest.

insurance.text: Medical care under Hungarian law, plus supplementary health insurance up to HUF 65,000/year (~€165).

travel.text: Not covered — travel to and from Hungary is not included.

duration: Funded for the full standard length of your programme, subject to meeting academic progression requirements each year.

eligibility.countries_note: Open to citizens of the 100+ sending-partner countries that hold a bilateral education agreement with Hungary — NOT to every nationality. Your country must currently be a sending partner, and you must be nominated by it.
eligibility.academic: You must have completed the level of education required for your target programme, with a strong academic record.
eligibility.age: No general age limit is stated (individual programmes may set their own).
eligibility.language: Proof of language ability (usually English, sometimes Hungarian) as required by your specific programme — check each programme's requirement.
eligibility.notes: Nomination by your sending partner (the Hungarian embassy, or the responsible ministry/agency in your country) is mandatory — only nominated applicants proceed.

requirements: Online application on apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu (up to 2 programme choices)
Certificate & transcripts for your prior studies
Language certificate as required by your chosen programme
Copy of your passport or ID
Any programme-specific documents (e.g. portfolio, or a research plan for PhD)

application.route: Two applications are required — the online Stipendium Hungaricum system AND your home-country sending partner.
steps: Check your country is a current sending partner, and contact them for their own process and deadline.
Register and apply online at apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu, choosing available programmes in the Study Finder.
Submit your application to your sending partner (embassy / ministry) — they nominate the candidates.
Nominated applications are reviewed by your chosen Hungarian institutions (their own admission requirements apply).
application.deadline_note: 15 January 2026, 14:00 CET for the online system (2026/27 cycle). Your sending partner's deadline may be earlier — confirm it with them.

important: You must be a citizen of a current sending-partner country AND be nominated — you can't apply on nationality alone.
Only programmes marked 'available' for your country in the Study Finder can be chosen.
The stipend is modest relative to living costs in Budapest; the housing contribution may not cover full rent.
You still need to meet each university's own admission requirements.
It runs on an annual cycle with a mid-January online deadline — prepare documents well ahead.
competition: Highly competitive — nominations per country are limited. No official acceptance rate is published.
universities_note: These are participating institutions we have in our catalogue. Stipendium Hungaricum has around 30 participating institutions in total — see the official institutions list for the complete, current set.

name: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship
provider: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (via Campus France)
tagline: France's prestige government scholarship for top international Master's and PhD students — but your French university must nominate you.
fields: Awarded in priority fields set each year (broadly sciences & engineering, economics & management, and law & political science). Confirm the current priority areas on Campus France.

tuition.text: Not covered by the grant. Some host institutions separately exempt Eiffel holders from tuition — confirm with the university.

stipend.text: Monthly allowance: €1,200 (Master's) and €2,100 (PhD), as of January 2026.

accommodation.text: Not paid, but the programme assists with finding housing.

travel.text: International and national transport are included.

duration: Master's: 12–36 months. PhD: a 12-month mobility period, which may be split into several stays.

eligibility.countries_note: Open to international (non-French) students. It cannot be held together with another French government grant.
eligibility.academic: An excellent academic record — institutions put forward only their strongest candidates.
eligibility.age: Age limit in the selection year: up to 29 for Master's, up to 35 for PhD.
eligibility.language: Language requirement depends on the programme (French or English).
eligibility.notes: You do NOT apply yourself — a French higher-education institution must submit your application. Contact the international office of the university you want to attend.

requirements: A French host institution willing to submit your application (this is essential)
A study/research project or motivation statement
Language proof as required by the programme

application.route: The French host institution applies on your behalf — students cannot apply directly to Campus France.
steps: Identify and contact a French institution's international office well before the deadline.
The institution assembles and submits your Eiffel application (there is an internal deadline, earlier than the national one).
Campus France and a selection committee review the nominated files.
Results are published (around end of March); admission to the programme is handled separately by the institution.
application.deadline_note: 8 January 2026 is the national submission deadline for institutions (call opened October 2025; results end of March). Your target institution's internal deadline is earlier — contact them first.

important: You can't apply yourself — a French institution must nominate you, so start with their international office.
The grant does not pay tuition (though some institutions waive it separately).
Age limits apply: ≤29 for Master's, ≤35 for PhD.
Priority fields are defined each year.
Highly competitive — each institution nominates only a few candidates.
competition: Highly competitive — institutions submit a limited number of candidates. No official acceptance rate is published.
universities_note: Eiffel is offered through participating French higher-education institutions, which nominate candidates — it is not tied to a fixed public list. Explore French universities and contact the international office of the one you're interested in.

name: Holland Scholarship (NL Scholarship)
provider: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science + participating institutions
tagline: A €5,000 first-year contribution for non-EEA students at participating Dutch universities.
fields: Most full-time bachelor's and master's programmes at participating Dutch institutions.

tuition.text: Not a full-tuition scholarship — tuition is not covered.

stipend.text: €5,000, paid once in your first year of study. It is a one-time contribution, not a recurring stipend.

duration: A one-time award in the first year of study.

eligibility.countries_note: Non-EEA nationality only (from outside the European Economic Area). You must not already hold a degree from a Dutch education institution.
eligibility.academic: You must meet the admission requirements of your chosen programme.
eligibility.language: As required by your programme (usually English).
eligibility.notes: Apply directly to the participating institution — each one runs its own selection and deadline.

requirements: An application/admission to a participating Dutch programme
The institution's own Holland Scholarship application (process varies by institution)

application.route: Apply directly to the participating institution — there is no central application.
steps: Choose a participating Dutch university and a full-time bachelor's or master's programme.
Check that institution's Holland Scholarship page for its process and deadline.
Apply for admission and for the scholarship as the institution directs.
application.deadline_note: No single deadline — each institution sets its own (applications for 2026/27 opened 1 November 2025). Common deadlines are 1 February or 1 May; confirm on your institution's page.

important: It's €5,000 once — a contribution toward your first year, not full funding.
You can't already hold a Dutch degree.
Each institution has its own deadline and selection — apply directly to them, not centrally.
competition: Competitive; each institution awards a limited number. No central acceptance rate is published.
universities_note: These are participating institutions the official page names; the scholarship runs at 11 Dutch research universities and 23 universities of applied sciences in total (2026/27) — see the official page for the full list, and explore all Dutch universities below.
